summary: Your tomato has early blight, a fungal disease that starts on the oldest leaves and works its way up. It is very treatable at this stage, but the sharp day-to-night temperature swing here leaves dew on the foliage every morning, which is exactly what the fungus needs to spread.

steps.action: Cut off every leaf showing brown target-shaped spots, along with the bare lower stems. Bag them and bin them — do not compost.
steps.why: Spores survive on fallen leaves and splash back up onto the plant with the next watering.

steps.action: Water at the soil line only, early in the morning.
steps.why: Morning water lets the leaves dry before nightfall. Evening or overhead watering keeps them wet right through the dew hours.

steps.action: Spread about 5cm of straw mulch over the soil around the base.
steps.why: It blocks soil splash, which is the main route spores travel back onto the lower leaves.

steps.action: Apply a copper-based fungicide, repeating every 7-10 days while symptoms are active.
steps.when: After pruning, on a still evening
steps.why: Copper is protective rather than curative — it shields the healthy leaves you just saved.

watchFor: Spots climbing past the middle of the plant despite treatment
Dark sunken patches appearing on the fruit itself
Yellowing that starts at the leaf tips rather than as distinct spots, which points to feeding rather than blight
